item.title: DJ Turner set to play for Bengals, Kyle Dugger ruled out
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Bengals have issued their injury designations for Sunday's game against the Falcons in Madrid.
item.content:encoded:
The Bengals have issued their injury designations for Sunday's game against the Falcons in Madrid.

Cornerback DJ Turner did not receive one of those designations. Turner was out of practice on Wednesday with a heel injury, but he's been a full participant the last two days and is set to play this weekend.

Safety Kyle Dugger will not play due to a quad injury. He has missed three of the last four games and did not participate in practice at all this week.

Defensive end Cedric Johnson is the team's only questionable player. He moved up to full participation on Friday after missing practice Wednesday and being listed as limited Thursday with ankle and foot injuries.

item.title: Minkah Fitzpatrick: No controversy with my quote, everyone on the Jets knows what I meant
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: After Sunday's loss to the Raiders, Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick said something that caused a bit of a controversy, but Fitzpatrick says there was no controversy with the only people who matter to him.
item.content:encoded:
After Sunday's loss to the Raiders, Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick said something that caused a bit of a controversy, but Fitzpatrick says there was no controversy with the only people who matter to him.

Fitzpatrick said what sounded like the loss was a case of the "Jets being Jets," but after that quote took off, the Jets told reporters that Fitzpatrick had actually said, “Jets beating Jets." Some thought Fitzpatrick was saying the Jets are fundamentally a bad franchise and that losing like they did is just who they are, but the Jets insisted Fitzpatrick was saying the Jets just need to cut down on their mistakes and stop beating themselves.

Asked about the quote on Thursday, Fitzpatrick said it's a non-issue with his teammates, and that's what's important to him.

"It hasn't really caused any stir within this locker room, and I think that's the most important thing. Everyone in this locker room knew what I was talking about," Fitzpatrick said. "Everybody within this locker room knew exactly what I said and what I was trying to communicate, and in my opinion that's all that matters."

Fitzpatrick said his teammates aren't upset and the focus is on winning on Sunday.

“I know what I said, and that's all I'm going to say," Fitzpatrick said. “It doesn’t matter. We’re playing Kansas City this week. The locker room knows what I said, or what I meant to say, however you want to put it. Either way, it doesn't matter. This locker room needs to focus on winning right now, and not something that I might have not said or something I might have done. Our focus and our objective now is to win and figure out what we need to win, not focus on shoulda, woulda, coulda.”

Ultimately, Fitzpatrick said, what the 2-6 Jets need is to get to 3-6 on Sunday.

item.title: NFLPA names Steelers LS Christian Kuntz their Community MVP for Week 9
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The NFL Players Association announced on Friday that they have named Steelers long snapper Christian Kuntz their Community MVP for Week 9 of the 2026 season.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL Players Association announced on Friday that they have named Steelers long snapper Christian Kuntz their Community MVP for Week 9 of the 2026 season.

Kuntz recently donated $10,000 to Pittsburgh Morrow school to help open a resource room that will benefit more than 200 students every month. Kuntz also helped stock that room with clothing and food while his foundation hosted its inaugural Kuntz 4 Ki6s Halloween Bash for 80 children from nine local nonprofit organizations.

“I am incredibly honored to be named this week’s NFLPA Community MVP,” Kuntz said. “Pittsburgh is home to me, and being able to make a positive impact in the community that I grew up in is extra special. Football has given us this platform, and I believe it's important to use that to make a difference beyond the field.”

The NFLPA will donate $10,000 to Kuntz's foundation and he will join the other weekly MVPs in being eligible for the Alan Page Award at the end of the season.

item.title: Jets rule out Garrett Wilson for Week 9
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Jets confirmed that they will be without wide receiver Garrett Wilson for Sunday's game in Kansas City.
item.content:encoded:
The Jets confirmed that they will be without wide receiver Garrett Wilson for Sunday's game in Kansas City.

Wilson is in the concussion protocol and did not practice on Wednesday and Thursday, so head coach Aaron Glenn's announcement about Wilson on Friday was an expected development. Sunday's game will be the first that Wilson has missed this season.

Wilson has 43 catches for 527 yards and three touchdowns on the season. Adonai Mitchell and rookie Omar Cooper will be the Jets' top wideouts this weekend.

Glenn said that running back Breece Hall (quad), linebacker David Bailey (groin), and tight end Mason Taylor (neck) are all set to play. Cornerback Nahshon Wright (back), linebacker Joseph Ossai (ankle), and defensive lineman Harrison Phillips (ankle) will be listed as questionable to face the Chiefs.

item.title: Ravens, Cardinals announce Jacoby Brissett trade
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Jacoby Brissett trade is done.
item.content:encoded:
The Jacoby Brissett trade is done.

The Ravens and Cardinals were said to be finalizing a deal that would send the veteran quarterback to Baltimore earlier this week. The trade was officially announced on Friday morning.

Neither team specified the draft compensation that will go to Arizona in exchange for Brissett, but Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that the Ravens will send a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-round pick to the Cardinals for Brissett and a 2027 5th-round pick.

Brissett started every game for the Cardinals this season before being demoted to the third team this week. Gardner Minshew is now the Cardinals starter with rookie Carson Beck in the No. 2 spot on the depth chart.

With Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley on injured reserve, the Ravens turned to undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano for Thursday night's loss to the Jaguars. Brissett will have over a week to familiarize himself with the team's offense before a Monday night game against the Chargers in Week 10.

item.title: NFL has not yet reinstated Brandon Aiyuk from reserve/left squad list
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: It's supposed to be a simple, administrative matter.
item.content:encoded:
It's supposed to be a simple, administrative matter. It apparently, in the case of 49ers receiver Brandon Aiyuk, is not.

Aiyuk reportedly filed the appropriate paperwork to be reinstated from the reserve/left squad list on Wednesday. His new agent, Drew Rosenhaus, tells PFT that the request was actually made on October 27.

Per the NFL, Aiyuk has not yet been reinstated.

The delay underscores the possibility that the NFL and the 49ers are working together to buy the team some time, especially if the team's goal is to recover up to $13 million without having to chase him around for it.

Again, it's supposed to be a simple process, like it was when Brett Favre applied for reinstatement from the reserve/retired list in 2008. It should be a simple box-checking exercise.

And with Aiyuk not reinstated, it complicates his plan to report to the team's facility on Friday. Although the 49ers are free to meet with Aiyuk and Rosenhaus, the 49ers will have no pressure to make a decision regarding what to do with Aiyuk unless and until the league office reinstates him.

item.title: Treveyon Henderson was hospitalized after "unexpected and unusual medical emergency"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Patriots running back Treveyon Henderson, who missed the Week 8 game against the Dolphins with an illness, remains absent from practice due to illness.
item.content:encoded:
Patriots running back Treveyon Henderson, who missed the Week 8 game against the Dolphins with an illness, remains absent from practice due to illness.

On Friday morning, Henderson posted a statement on social media regarding his health situation.

"Recently, I experienced an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms that required hospitalization for several days," Henderson said. "During that time, I underwent extensive medical testing and evaluation. While the results of my comprehensive medical testing have come back positive and reassuring, the cause of this remains unknown and unexplainable.

"I will continue working closely with specialists and physical therapists to focus on my recovery, as these symptoms have affected my strength, coordination, and some of my physical functions. I am committed to doing everything necessary to return to full health.

"My health and long-term well-being remain my foremost priorities.

"I want to thank my wife for being by my side throughout all of this, and most importantly, I want to thank Jesus for giving me a peace that surpasses all understanding. Despite all of this, my heart rejoices in The Lord and my heart is at peace knowing that He is always faithful and His promise of Romans 8:28 always remain true. 'And we know that all things work together for good to those who love God, to those who are the called according to His purpose.' The purpose of trials in life is not to drive us away from God, but to only bring us closer. May God's Will be done, not mine.

"My wife and I are deeply grateful for family and loved ones, the New England Patriots organization, my agent, my medical team, teammates, and everyone who has offered prayers, encouragement, and support.

"We respectfully ask for continued prayers and privacy as we focus on my health and recovery."

Based on the Week 8 injury report, which first listed Henderson as having an illness on Thursday, the situation occurred between Wednesday's practice and Thursday's practice. Based on his statement, he could be out for a while; if his "strength, coordination, and some of [his] physical functions" have been undermined, it's hard to envision him safely playing professional football.

We wish Henderson the best as he recovers, and as he tries to understand what occurred.

item.title: Jaguars' point differential of +108 this season is 50 points better than any other team
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Jaguars have won four games by more than 21 points this season; no other team has more than one win by more than 21 points.
item.content:encoded:
No NFL team is dominating opponents like the Jacksonville Jaguars.

After blowing out the Ravens 33-10 on Thursday night, the Jaguars have now outscored their opponents by a cumulative score of 229-121 this season. That's a point differential of +108, by far the best in the NFL.

The team with the second-best point differential in the NFL is the 49ers, at +58. The Jaguars' point differential is 50 points better than the next-best team.

At 6-2, the Jaguars do not have the best record in the league, as the Bills, 49ers and Vikings are all 6-1. The 49ers are favored to beat the Raiders and improve to 7-1, and the Bills and Vikings play each other on Monday night, so the winner will be 7-1.

But at the midway point of the season, point differential is a better indication of a team's quality, and a better predictor of a team's future success, than win-loss record. That's because with as small a sample size as half a season, a few plays in a few close games can skew the won-loss record, but a few plays don't skew point differential. Historically, the teams that prove to be the best over the course of a season are the teams that win some blowouts, even if they also lose some close games.

Winning blowouts and losing close games is exactly what the Jaguars do. Both of the Jaguars' losses were one-possession games that were tied in the fourth quarter, while the Jaguars' wins have included some massive blowouts: The Jaguars' 35-point win over the Colts was the biggest blowout of this NFL season, their 29-point win over the Patriots was the fourth-biggest blowout in the NFL this season, their 24-point win over the Browns was the seventh-biggest blowout in the NFL this season, and Thursday night's 23-point win over the Ravens was the 11th-biggest blowout in the NFL this season.

The Jaguars have won four games by more than 21 points this season; no other team has more than one win by more than 21 points.

Jacksonville has a 3.5-game lead in the AFC South, and six of the Jaguars' nine remaining games are against opponents with a losing record. They're poised to run away with their division, perhaps earn the No. 1 seed in the AFC, and maybe blow some teams out in the playoffs just like they have in the regular season.

item.title: Jared Verse was upset that Browns teammates didn't react when he took a cheap shot
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Browns defensive end Jared Verse was picked up and thrown to the ground by Steelers guard Mason McCormick on Sunday, and McCormick wasn't the only person Verse was upset with afterward.
item.content:encoded:
Browns defensive end Jared Verse was picked up and thrown to the ground by Steelers guard Mason McCormick on Sunday, and McCormick wasn't the only person Verse was upset with afterward.

Verse told reporters in Cleveland today that he was upset both by McCormick's cheap shot and by his teammates' reaction, or lack thereof. Verse thought the rest of the Browns' players should have had his back, and didn't.

"To be quite honest with you, that was the play that made me really angry," Verse said. "I was already upset about the game, the way things were moving, but at that point it became deep. You're doing dirty shit, you're trying to sweep my legs out. That honestly could have put me in a position to not be able to finish the season, put me in a position to change my life in a very bad aspect, so that upset me. The lack of reaction by those around me had upset me a lot. They were focused on the game and everything like that, but a similar play happened to Derek Barnett on the next field goal, and I spazzed, I lost it. Because those are my brothers, those are my teammates, and when you do something like that to them, it upsets me deeply. We have to get better, we have to be aware. These are my teammates, these are my brothers, and we're not fighting for each other."

Verse said he addressed his feelings with his teammates. Verse did acknowledge that he brought some of it on himself by the trash talk he was directing at the Steelers, but he still felt that his teammates should have protected him when it escalated from verbal to physical.

“That's a conversation that we've had, we've spoken about," Verse said. "I made my concerns known, I’ve made my issues known about the situation, but also, I didn't put them in a position to let them know that, I didn't let them know beforehand I was going to talk to the Steelers and Steeler Nation. I've got to be better.”

Verse, the 2024 NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year who arrived in Cleveland in the trade that sent Myles Garrett to the Rams, has been a disappointment this season. His teammates may be wishing he'd focus a little less on talking trash and getting into altercations on the field, and a little more on sacking the opposing quarterback — something he hasn't done yet this season.

item.title: Trevor Lawrence is having by far the best season of his career
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Trevor Lawrence has so much talent for the quarterback position that if freshmen could declare for the NFL draft, Lawrence probably would have been the first overall pick in 2019, when he had just led Clemson to a national championship as a true freshman.
item.content:encoded:
Trevor Lawrence has so much talent for the quarterback position that if freshmen could declare for the NFL draft, Lawrence probably would have been the first overall pick in 2019, when he had just led Clemson to a national championship as a true freshman. Instead, Lawrence stayed three years at Clemson and was the first pick in 2021, viewed as a sure-thing quarterback prospect.

In Year 6, Lawrence finally looks like everything he was supposed to be.

Lawrence is having by far the best year of his NFL career, with career-high stats across the board that are constrained only by the fact that the Jaguars win so many blowouts that Lawrence doesn't throw many passes in the fourth quarter.

So far this season, Lawrence has completed 146 of 224 passes for 1,932 yards, with 18 touchdowns, four interceptions and an NFL-leading passer rating of 111.7. Project Lawrence's totals to a 17-game season, and he's on pace to finish with 4,106 yards, 38 touchdowns and nine interceptions. Those are MVP numbers.

Lawrence's rookie year was a disaster, as he led the league in interceptions while playing on a chaotic Jaguars team coached by Urban Meyer, whose only foray into NFL coaching lasted less than one season. Lawrence and the Jaguars got a lot better once they kicked Meyer to the curb, but even in the next three years with Doug Pederson, an offensive coach with a Super Bowl-winning pedigree, Lawrence didn't live up to the pre-draft hype.

Playing in Liam Coen's offense, something has changed. Last year the Jaguars went 13-4, winning double-digit games for the first time since drafting Lawrence, and this year Lawrence and the Jaguars are even better. Lawrence's average of 8.6 yards per pass is the best of his career by almost a yard and a half, a remarkable improvement for any quarterback to make in his sixth season.

Lawrence has thrown touchdown passes on 8 percent of his attempts, the best in the NFL this season and by far the best mark of his career. And after getting sacked a career-high 41 times last year, Lawrence has gotten much more comfortable reading the pass rush in his second year in Coen's offense and has only been sacked 13 times this season.

Lawrence's numbers would look even better if the Jaguars weren't so often taking their foot off the gas late in games because they're blowing opponents out. Lawrence has 1,196 yards and 12 touchdowns in the first halves of games this season, but he only has 736 yards and six touchdowns in the second halves of games.

The Jaguars currently have the fourth-best odds to win the Super Bowl, and Lawrence has the fifth-best odds to win MVP. That might be underselling them, and him. The Jaguars may just be the best team, with the best quarterback, in the NFL right now.

item.title: Jaguars LB Foye Oluokun: We can't let wins mask stuff
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Jaguars have taken two more steps toward the playoffs over the last two weeks and they've done it in impressive fashion.
item.content:encoded:
The Jaguars have taken two more steps toward the playoffs over the last two weeks and they've done it in impressive fashion.

They followed up a 42-7 humiliation of the Colts in Week 8 with Thursday night's 33-10 rout of the Ravens on the road. Blowouts are nothing new for the Jags as they have outscored their opponents by 108 points over their eight games this season and their 6-2 record has them well positioned to win the AFC South.

Winning another division title is not the team's goal, however, and linebacker Foye Oluokun focused on that when he spoke to reporters on Thursday night.

“You win and it feels great. We can’t let wins mask stuff," Oluokun said. "You’ve always got stuff to improve. I've been here a while, went through winning, winning, winning, and one season, we let a lot slide because we were winning. So we got to keep learning in wins and stuff because it's all about who's playing the best in December and then we make that run [in] January and February. We got to keep improving all the way through the year, get the advantageous situation going into the playoffs."

The Jaguars hosted a playoff game after winning 13 games in 2025, but they were bounced out of the postseason by the Bills. Oluokun was on the field during that game and avoiding a similar outcome will be front and center as he tries to keep the Jaguars' focus in the right place while they are running roughshod over weaker clubs.

item.title: As Chargers' offense struggles, Mike McDaniel will move from the sideline to the booth
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel will get a different perspective on his struggling offense on Sunday against the Texans.
item.content:encoded:
Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel will get a different perspective on his struggling offense on Sunday against the Texans.

McDaniel said today that he will move upstairs to the booth to call plays after previously working from the sideline.

“One of the things that I want to try is call plays from the box to see adjustments for myself and communicate with the position coaches appropriately what things we can focus on between series,” McDaniel said. "I won't be in the same spot."

Although the Chargers' offense has been among the worst in the NFL this season and head coach Jim Harbaugh has faced questions about whether he should fire his offensive coordinator, McDaniel insisted that he's not concerned about the criticism.

"My problem solving doesn't come from insecurity," McDaniel said. "I'm not trying to prove or justify anything."

The Chargers rank dead last in the NFL in scoring, having scored only 99 points this season, and they have an NFL-high 17 turnovers. McDaniel said he thinks it's worth trying something different while delegating some of what he had been doing on the sideline to the assistant coaches.

“Seems like a good action to take based on how things have gone this year, and realistically something that I’ve only brought up because I've observed, I’m very confident in the rest of the offensive coaching staff and how they’re able to set the tone and communicate information on the sidelines. So I feel a little more comfortable to try that," McDaniel said.

If that doesn't work, Harbaugh's next step might be to move McDaniel from the booth to the unemployment line.

item.title: Jonathan Taylor: No one likes uncertainty
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Colts running back Jonathan Taylor has spent the last two weeks fielding questions about whether he'll remain with the team and that will come to an end by next Tuesday one way or another.
item.content:encoded:
Colts running back Jonathan Taylor has spent the last two weeks fielding questions about whether he'll remain with the team and that will come to an end by next Tuesday one way or another.

Taylor will either remain with the Colts through Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET trade deadline or he'll be dealt to a team that thinks he can help push them over the top this season. Until he's dealt or the deadline passes, Taylor knows "you're not going to avoid" the questions he faced one again on Thursday and he knows that he'll be happy when they stop coming his way.

"No one wants uncertainty," Taylor said Thursday, via Stephen Holder of ESPN.com. "Until the past couple weeks, it's kind of been the same thing. But it won't be until Tuesday where you'll know exactly what's going on, you'll know exactly what the verdict is."

Taylor played amid the rumors in last week's loss to the Jaguars and the plan is for him to play against the Cowboys this week. He said he is working to keep his focus on that game because he doesn't "want external factors creeping in and trying to alter your play," but that will be a much easier task to accomplish once there's certainty about where he'll be after November 10.

item.title: Derrick Henry: I haven't mentioned going somewhere else, let's try to get better
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Ravens got blown out for the third straight game on Thursday night and they lost their fourth straight overall, which led running back Derrick Henry to call it the "same story" after the Jaguars rolled to a 33-10 win in Baltimore.
item.content:encoded:
The Ravens got blown out for the third straight game on Thursday night and they lost their fourth straight overall, which led running back Derrick Henry to call it the "same story" after the Jaguars rolled to a 33-10 win in Baltimore.

Lamar Jackson only saw brief playing time in one of those losses, so the Ravens have been starting games in a hole throughout their losing streak. Jackson may not be back this season and that makes it hard to see any reason why the story that's frustrating Henry is going to change before the year is out. Given the stage Henry's at in his career, it wasn't unusual that he was asked after the game if he was reconsidering his plan to remain with the Ravens until he hangs up his cleats.

Henry said that he isn't thinking about changing uniforms.

"I have not mentioned me going anywhere else," Henry said, via a transcript from the team. "I'm saying, 'Let's go back to work. Let's try to get better and turn this thing around."

The trade deadline is Tuesday and any team looking to bolster their backfield could do a lot worse than adding one of the most prolific backs in the history of the league. While a move may not be Henry's first choice, it could turn out to be the best course of action for the Ravens and he might find he likes being back on a team that can seriously talk about contending during the second half of the season.

item.title: The Vikings should explore a trade for Daniel Jones
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Kevin O'Connell's decision to punt with 3:01 to play speaks volumes about the level of trust in Kyler Murray.
item.content:encoded:
At a time when the Vikings are believed to be talking to the Colts about a potential trade for running back Jonathan Taylor, they should adjust their focal point, just a bit.

The Vikings should be talking to the Colts about a potential trade for quarterback Daniel Jones.

When the thought first popped into my somewhat relaxed brain on Sunday, I was mostly kidding. After reflecting on Sunday's 19-15 loss to the Lions — and revisiting the rare displays of frustration from receiver Justin Jefferson late in the game and, even more significantly, from coach Kevin O'Connell when talking to quarterback Kyler Murray after an ugly interception late in the first half — it's not a joke.

They should immediately pivot from Taylor to Jones.

The Vikings had Jones in the building two years ago, after he was released by the Giants. They wanted to keep him for 2025, more (by all appearances) than they wanted to keep Sam Darnold. (Indeed, there were whispers of a potential benching of Darnold for Jones in the 2024 postseason.)

Now that the Colts are in full-blown pre-rebuild mode, trading Jones should be part of the effort to clear the decks (and stockpile picks) for the next G.M. And while the Colts have a window to avoid more than $10 million of Jones's $38 million compensation package for 2027 via a trade in the early days of the new league year in March, they could get more now from a contender that envisions Jones as an immediate upgrade.

Jones obviously won't be the long-term answer in Indianapolis. And he would undoubtedly welcome the chance to move on from a team that prematurely threw in the towel last week by trading guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner.

In Minnesota, Jones would be an immediate upgrade over Kyler Murray. The difference between Jones vs. Murray could be more significant than the difference between Jonathan Taylor and Aaron Jones/Jordan Mason. Which, if accurate, would result in a bigger overall bump to the offense.

The Vikings have a championship-caliber defense, thanks in large part to the work of defensive coordinator Brian Flores. The grind-it-out-and-get-a-win formula had been working — until it didn't.

Here's the inescapable reality. When they win with quarterback play that is inconsistent and, in turn, frustrating to people like Jefferson and O'Connell, it's easy to overlook the flaws and keep pushing forward. When they lose, the frustrations of that moment become compounded by the lingering frustrations regarding plays and points left on the field in the wins that were salvaged by the defense.

Whether it's Jones or someone else (including a possible pivot to Carson Wentz), O'Connell and G.M. Nolan Teasley need to conduct a frank, candid, and objective assessment of the quarterback play under Murray. The fact that they picked Murray over J.J. McCarthy shouldn't be a factor. That's the kind of pride/ego consideration that keeps dysfunctional teams dysfunctional by doubling down on a mistake instead of admitting it and moving on.

The Vikings need to realize that: (1) the defense is great; (2) the running game is good enough; and (3) the passing game is too spotty to be expected to make a big play in a big spot.

Consider the decision that O'Connell made with 3:01 to play on Sunday, when the Vikings faced fourth and five from their own 33. Down four points after the Detroit running game had hot-knife-through-buttered their way to the go-ahead touchdown, why give the ball back to the Lions and let them close out the game by continuing to lean on Jahmyr Gibbs?

In that moment, O'Connell thought the chances of winning were enhanced by punting — not by asking the offense to gain five yards in a gotta-have-it situation.

While the choice showed unwarranted confidence in the defense, it showed NO confidence in the quarterback.

Frankly, that one specific decision from O'Connell leads naturally to the next, more consequential decision that the organization must make. If O'Connell doesn't trust the offense under Murray to gain five yards with the game on the line, the Vikings should no longer entrust the offense to Murray.

It's that simple. And, if the Vikings hope to avoid an outcome to the season that will result in an every-other-year playoff appearance and another one-and-done postseason, they'll make the decision that someone other than Murray should be playing quarterback.

At a time when politics have become a major national focal point, this would be a so-called 80-20 issue among Vikings fans. They've seen the "just good enough is just good enough" movie for decades. With the defense the Vikings currently have, the offense needs more. If they're serious about having a snowball's chance in San Diego to get back to the Super Bowl for the first time in 50 years, they'll send Kyler to Belize and make a play for Jones.

Or someone else. See if the Raiders are willing to part with Kirk Cousins (they shouldn't be, but why not make the call?) Call the Chargers about Justin Herbert. Scour every depth chart and start doing the due diligence.

When Cousins suffered a season-ending torn Achilles tendon just before the trade deadline in 2023, the Vikings mobilized instantly to find a replacement. Based on the full body of work from Murray to date in 2026, they should be doing the same thing now — if they want to parlay their 6-0 start into the best possible finish.

item.title: Bill Belichick, Tom Coughlin among five coaches to advance in Hall of Fame selection process
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Bill Belichick fell short of the necessary votes to be elected to the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2026, but he may have another chance in 2027.
item.content:encoded:
Bill Belichick fell short of the necessary votes to be elected to the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2026, but he may have another chance in 2027.

The Hall of Fame announced the five coaches who have advanced to the next round of consideration in the current selection process. One of those coaches will be selected for consideration by the full selection committee ahead of the Super Bowl.

Belichick is joined by Tom Coughlin, Mike Holmgren, Dan Reeves, and Mike Shanahan. All five coaches also advanced to this point in the selection process last year. This is the fourth time that Holmgren has advanced to this point.

Don Coryell was the last coach selected for the Hall of Fame. He was part of the Class of 2023.

item.title: Kyler Murray out for Monday vs. Bills, week-to-week with hamstring injury
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Carson Wentz will make his second start of the season in place of the injured Murray.
item.content:encoded:
Kyler Murray's hamstring injury is serious enough that it will sideline him for at least a week.

Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell told reporters in his Thursday press conference that Murray is out for Monday night's game against the Bills with a hamstring strain and is considered week-to-week.

Carson Wentz will start Week 9, which will be his second start of the season.

"For [Murray], his movement skills, and the way he plays the game, we do feel like we’d be putting him at risk of possibly turning this into a more significant injury than it is by trying to have him work through it here early on," O'Connell said. "So, Carson will start the football game and Max [Brosmer] will back him up."

While it didn't seem like O'Connell was too concerned about Murray's availability earlier in the week, further testing revealed the extent of the issue.

"I think hamstrings are always unique," O'Connell said. "[Y]ou always have to understand that whatever that picture or that imaging says, sometimes it’s an injury you can really hone in on. That’s why I wanted to be certain before I went speculating on Monday just because I wanted to be sure it wasn’t something that would prohibit him from playing — until it was.

"I’m not going to get into the details of the grade or the injury or the level medically speaking, but just knowing that Kyler needs his mobility — it’s a big, huge part of what makes him an effective player. If that puts him at risk of potentially adding to the grade of the injury, we can’t do that. It’s a long season. We hope to get him back and get him going."

O'Connell noted injured reserve is not a consideration for Murray with this injury.

Wentz stepped in and played after Murray suffered a concussion earlier this season. Wentz completed 23-of-39 passes against the Packers and Bears for 276 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions.

“Obviously, there’s a ton of confidence in Carson,” O’Connell said. “He’s had a major, major role in two wins this year against two really good teams. He’s a steadying presence and a guy we know can go in and play good football, that’s why we feel so great about having him here.

“He’s going to throw a lot of completions. He’s going to put the ball in play. He’s got such a high, high understanding of not only the offense but what he’s looking at on the other side. He has 100 games of experience. He’s the perfect guy in a moment where you can’t have Kyler out there at full strength to go in there. And we feel very strongly about when Carson’s in there, we’re going to get really effective quarterback play.”

Minnesota’s offense has struggled to generate yards and points this season, with the club ranking No. 27 in scoring and No. 29 in total yards. We’ll see if Wentz can provide a spark to change that on Monday night.

item.title: Jesse Minter: I told Ravens' players there are no excuses
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: No team in the NFL has been as bad as the Ravens recently: Baltimore is on a four-game losing streak, and has lost three consecutive games by more than 21 points apiece.
item.content:encoded:
No team in the NFL has been as bad as the Ravens recently: Baltimore is on a four-game losing streak, and has lost three consecutive games by more than 21 points apiece. Ravens coach Jesse Minter wants his players to know that getting blown out every week is not OK.

The Ravens have been playing without star quarterback Lamar Jackson, and since last week they've been without backup quarterback Tyler Huntley as well, but Minter says that's no excuse. Minter says there is no excuse at all.

"Obviously, [it's] a tough situation for our guys, but I just told them there’s no excuses, there's no whatever, 'We don't have this guy; we don't have that guy,'" Minter said. "The results are not acceptable for us and what we're after."

Minter said he still thinks he can win with the players he has.

"I believe in our guys," Minter said. "There's spurts of good enough football. There is a real inconsistency, I would say, at all three levels, all three phases. And again, some of that is due to whatever, but that is what it is. Nobody cares about that stuff."

What everyone cares about is winning, and the Ravens aren't doing that. Not even close.

item.title: The Brandon Aiyuk return is complicated by the money he owes the 49ers
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: On the surface, receiver Brandon Aiyuk's effort to become a free agent should be easy.
item.content:encoded:
On the surface, receiver Brandon Aiyuk's effort to become a free agent should be easy. At a deeper level, the question is whether the 49ers will try to complicate the situation, in an effort to delay or to prevent Aiyuk from picking his next team with no trade compensation to the 49ers.

One potential motivation to frustrate his efforts is pride. If Aiyuk goes to another team and re-establishes himself as a high-level player, it will make the 49ers look even more foolish for giving him a massive contract at a time when they had a trade to the Steelers on the tee.

Another potential motivation is good, old-fashioned spite. Aiyuk constantly needled the team on social media this summer, culminating in a post that made fun of coach Kyle Shanahan's pre-training camp car crash. The 49ers could be tempted to try to keep him from signing with a new team simply because they can — and because they feel no obligation or inclination to do him any favors.

The third, and perhaps best, motivation is money. Aiyuk arguably defaulted on his contract, making the team eligible to recover a sizable chunk of the money it paid him. A Thursday night tweet from Tom Pelissero of Netflix points to the effort to recoup bonus money as the potential basis for an effort to place a major roadblock in Aiyuk's path to a new team.

Said Pelissero: "Veteran WR Brandon Aiyuk owes the 49ers roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture — a potential complication in his efforts to secure his release by reporting to the facility Friday. The NFL Management Council and the NFL Players Association are both involved in attempting to resolve the situation. The sides could reach an agreement to pay back the money, or it could go to arbitration. But it’s complicated and may take time to resolve."

In other words, "F—k you, pay me."

The 49ers, in collaboration with the league, seem to be devising a way to avoid the otherwise simple application of the roster rules. One, Aiyuk files for reinstatement from the reserve/left squad list. Two, the league reinstates him. Three, the 49ers have to decide whether to put him on the 53-man roster (at a prorated base salary of $26.015 million) or release him.

Reinstatement from the reserve/left squad is supposed to be administrative. The NFL's daily transaction report has yet to mention Aiyuk's reinstatement.

It could be that the league (in a Brendan Sorsby-style move) is tapping the brakes on reinstatement as an effort to leverage a repayment agreement from Aiyuk. Should it be that way? No. Will that stop the NFL from doing whatever it chooses to do? Also no.

The mere fact that the Pelissero tweet links the two issues proves that the 49ers are at least considering, if not already implementing, a strategy that consists of not letting Aiyuk go until Aiyuk agrees to repay all or part of the $13 million that they believe he owes. And, if he doesn't, he may not get the contractual freedom he seeks.

He'd have possible recourse under the Collective Bargaining Agreement. But that process would take time to resolve. And, through it all, the remaining weeks of the 2026 regular season will pass without Aiyuk able to join a new team.

Bottom line? The sooner he agrees to cough up enough cash to satisfy the 49ers, the sooner he'll have a chance to play for a new team.

item.title: Thursday Night Football: Jaguars blow out Ravens 33-10
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Jaguars outgained the Ravens 319 to 227 and forced three Baltimore turnovers.
item.content:encoded:
The Jaguars didn't eat the cheese. They didn't overlook the Ravens.

Jacksonville cruised to a 33-10 victory, moving to 6-2. Baltimore lost its fourth consecutive game to fall to 4-5.

Without starting quarterback Lamar Jackson and backup Tyler Huntley, and with undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano making his first start, the Ravens' game plan was simple: Run the ball and shorten the game. They didn't stand a chance despite 34 runs and 19 passes and a slight edge in time of possession (30:45 to 29:15).

The Jaguars won for the eighth time by 20-plus points since the start of last season.

The Ravens didn't have a first down in the second half until Justice Hill ran for a 65-yard touhdown with 7:15 remaining. Baltimore ended with three first downs in the second half and 10 for the game.

The Jaguars outgained the Ravens 319 to 227, and the visitors forced Baltimore into three turnovers. Jourdan Lewis and Montaric Brown each had an interception of Fagnano, and linebacker Jalen McLeod forced and recovered a fumble by LaJohntay Wester on a kickoff.

Fagnano finished 10-of-18 for 60 yards and two interceptions. Hill had nine carries for 85 yards, and Henry moved up to seventh on the NFL's all-time rushing list with 57 yards on 17 carries.

Lawrence went 16-of-26 for 242 yards and a touchdown. Jakobi Meyers had four catches for 65 yards; rookie tight end Nate Boerkircher caught two passes for 61 yards; and Parker Washington had two catches for 61 yards and a touchdown.

Bhayshul Tuten had 12 carries for 29 yards and a touchdown, and Ameer Abdullah had seven carries for 30 yards.

item.title: Falcons list James Pearce, Divine Diablo as questionable for Sunday
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich said this week that the Falcons plan to use linebacker James Pearce in a pass rushing role against the Bengals in Madrid this Sunday, but the team didn't guarantee he'll be playing on their final injury report of the week.
item.content:encoded:
Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich said this week that the Falcons plan to use linebacker James Pearce in a pass rushing role against the Bengals in Madrid this Sunday, but the team didn't guarantee he'll be playing on their final injury report of the week.

Pearce is listed as questionable to play in his first week back from an eight-game suspension. Pearce was a full participant in practice this week and was not dealing with any injury earlier in the week, but the team listed him with a back issue on Friday. They will have to formally add him to the active roster in order for him to be in the lineup in Week 9.

The Falcons also listed linebacker Divine Deablo (forearm) as questionable to return after missing the last two games. Deablo was also a full participant in practice.

Linebacker Yasir Abdullah (hamstring), defensive back Billy Bowman (hamstring), wide receiver Beaux Collins (hip), and offensive tackle Cameron Williams (ankle) are also listed as questionable after full practice participation.

Wide receiver Zachariah Branch (hamstring) was ruled out earlier this week and did not travel to Spain. Running back Brian Robinson (hamstring) was ruled out on Friday.

item.title: 2026 NFL Trade Deadline live updates: Tracker, deals, news, rumors, analysis
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Jeffery Simmons, DeForest Buckner, Quenton Nelson and more big-name NFL players are on the move.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL trade deadline is at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, November 10, and PFT has you covered with news and analysis of every trade, potential trade, rumor of a trade and trade that won’t be happening.

Here’s what’s happening on the NFL trade front:

Derrick Henry says he's not thinking about changing teams: The Ravens star expressed a desire to help the team improve after a fourth-straight loss.

Jacoby Brissett is headed to Baltimore: The Ravens and Cardinals are finalizing a deal involving the veteran quarterback.

Jonathan Taylor wants to know where he'll finish the season: Taylor said no one likes uncertainty when asked about talk that the Colts will trade him.

Chargers say they're not trading Khalil Mack: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said, "I want Khalil Mack to be here and Khalil Mack wants to be here."

Jeffery Simmons to Bears: Chicago receives Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Tennessee will receive 2027 and 2028 first-round picks along with a fourth-round pick in 2027.

Quenton Nelson to Seahawks: The Seahawks will send a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick back to Indianapolis.

DeForest Buckner to 49ers: Indianapolis will receive a 2027 fourth-round pick from San Francisco.

Jonathan Taylor trade talks have picked up: The Colts may not be done making deals.

The Jets have reportedly rebuffed Garrett Wilson trade interest: The Jets are not expected to deal their top wideout.

The Colts are open for business: Indianapolis is building for the future after firing General Manager Chris Ballard. Jonathan Taylor hasn’t requested a trade. Josh Downs says he's "open to whatever."

Budda Baker's name surfaces in trade rumors: Baker says he hasn’t asked to be traded from Arizona and also hasn't asked not to be traded.

Brian Thomas is a name to watch: The Jaguars trading Thomas frequently comes up in trade rumors.

Garrett Wilson wants to remain a Jet: The talented receiver says he is hoping not to get traded.

item.title: Derrick Henry's production has plummeted without Lamar Jackson this season
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Without quarterback Lamar Jackson, the Ravens want to be able to rely on running back Derrick Henry.
item.content:encoded:
Without quarterback Lamar Jackson, the Ravens want to be able to rely on running back Derrick Henry. That plan isn't working.

In Thursday night's 33-10 loss to the Jaguars, Henry managed just 57 yards on 17 carries. That continues what has been happening all season, with Henry struggling to get anything going without Jackson on the field.

It was a bad omen in Week 4 against the Titans, when Jackson left at halftime with an ankle injury and Henry was ineffective in the second half. In the first half of that game, with Jackson on the field, Henry had seven carries for 38 yards, an average of 5.4 yards per carry, and a touchdown. In the second half with Tyler Huntley, Henry had 16 carries for 35 yards, an average of 2.2 yards per carry, and no touchdowns.

Jackson has played one snap since that Titans game, and the story has been the same, with Henry not able to do much of anything.

Overall this season, in three and a half games playing with Jackson, Henry has 73 carries for 339 yards, an average of 4.6 yards per carry and 97 yards per game, and seven touchdowns. In five and a half games without Jackson, Henry has 102 carries for 350 yards, an average of 3.4 yards per carry and 64 yards per game, and one touchdown.

At 4-5 and in last place in the AFC North, the Ravens, who entered the year with Super Bowl aspirations, are on the verge of their season collapsing. They need to turn things around, and they need Henry to turn things around.

item.title: Justin Jefferson says his frustration came from "wanting to win"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Vikings receiver Justin Jefferson engaged in a rare display of frustration late in Sunday's 19-15 loss to the Lions.
item.content:encoded:
Vikings receiver Justin Jefferson engaged in a rare display of frustration late in Sunday's 19-15 loss to the Lions. He also didn't talk to reporters after the game, possibly to avoid saying things that would underscore what he was feeling in the moment.

Four days later, Jefferson spoke to the media — and the No. 1 topic was his apparent mood during Minnesota's first loss of the season.

"It was wanting to win," Jefferson said, via Kevin Seifert of ESPN, "and I felt like we had plenty of opportunities to win that game and we only hurt ourselves in multiple ways. It's just wanting better from the whole entire offense especially. And I feel like the potential and the guys that we have in that room is something very, very special. I feel like we're wasting that if not going out there executing the plays that we have called and just not living to that standard that we feel like we live up to every single day."

Jefferson, who always says all the right things about his quarterbacks, said all the right things about Kyler Murray, whose performance against Detroit largely contributed to the failure to score more than 15 points.

"I feel like Kyler has continued to grow," Jefferson said. "I feel like Kyler is continuing to get comfortable with this offense. And I feel like the plays that are there are plays that he's well capable of making. And those are plays that we've seen him make multiple times throughout the season, throughout practice and in training camp as well. So we definitely have faith in him. We have confidence in him to go out there and be that guy that we need him and want him to be.

"But all in all, it's just executing our plays and just coming ready to play. And I feel like once he's back out there and he gets more comfortable with the system, more comfortable with just throwing to these different type of receivers, then I feel like he's going to look a lot better in [reporters'] eyes. But we see that every single day. We see that type of Kyler that we need out there on Sundays every single day. So just bringing that on Sundays. We're behind him. We're confident in him, so we just going to keep riding with him."

For now, the Vikings will ride with Carson Wentz, while Murray is out with a hamstring injury. And Wentz has proven that, of all the quarterbacks who have played for the Vikings since Sam Darnold left for Seattle after the 2024 season, Wentz knows how to get the ball to Jefferson.

Soft bench or not, Wentz has an opportunity to stay on the field if he makes the plays that Murray didn't on Sunday. Plays that, by the time the game was on the line, coach Kevin O'Connell didn't allow Murray to try to make.

The one moment that resonates from Sunday's game wasn't anything Murray did or failed to do. It came from O'Connell's decision to punt from the Minnesota 33-yard line on fourth and five with 3:01 to play. Given the manner in which the Lions were running the ball, the likelihood of getting another opportunity to score a touchdown was slim.

Put simply, if O'Connell didn't trust Murray to gain five yards with the game on the line, O'Connell shouldn't entrust the starting job to Murray.

For now, Murray technically can't play due to injury. It's hard not to wonder whether, if Murray had made the plays needed to outscore the Lions on Sunday, he'd be playing on Monday night despite the injured hamstring.

item.title: George Kittle is skeptical that Brandon Aiyuk will "get in" the team facility
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: As 49ers receiver Brandon Aiyuk attempts to lay the foundation for a return to the NFL, at least one other 49ers player has expressed skepticism about Aiyuk's plan.
item.content:encoded:
As 49ers receiver Brandon Aiyuk attempts to lay the foundation for a return to the NFL, at least one other 49ers player has expressed skepticism about Aiyuk's plan.

His new agent, Drew Rosenhaus, has said that Aiyuk will report to the 49ers' facility on Friday. Tight end George Kittle shared his views regarding that strategy on Thursday when asked whether he's looking forward to seeing Aiyuk.

"Do you think he gets in the facility?" Kittle said, via Grant Cohn of SI.com.

Kittle then was asked if he thinks Aiyuk gets into the facility.

"Plead the fifth," Kittle said. "Yeah. You can ask [G.M.] John [Lynch]. Or [coach] Kyle [Shanahan]. Don't ask me. I'm a conspiracy guy."

"Is there a conspiracy?" Kittle was asked.

"Plead the fifth," he said.

Kittle's skepticism is warranted. The entire situation is strange, and awkward. Aiyuk clearly hopes to trigger his outright release by reporting for work, after months of making it clear he had no intention to do so.

The 49ers are tiptoeing around the situation, for now. Before the team has to do anything, Aiyuk needs to check the various boxes that put the 49ers in a posture that requires a decision.

Of all potential outcomes, the least likely involves Aiyuk being welcomed back onto the roster. Especially since Aiyuk likely has no desire to be on the roster.

He wants his freedom, and he finally — after months of stubbornness — has initiated the process aimed at making that happen. While it's possible that the 49ers will search for a hardball outcome that involves keeping him from becoming a free agent while avoiding putting him back on the team, the chances of Aiyuk wandering around the locker room and eventually wearing a 49ers' helmet again seem to be incredibly slim.

item.title: Ravens rule out Kyle Hamilton with a hip injury
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton was injured in the second quarter and briefly returned after halftime.
item.content:encoded:
Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton was injured in the second quarter and briefly returned after halftime. His night, though, is finished.

The Ravens ruled out Hamilton with a hip injury.

He has three tackles, including a tackle for loss, and a pass defensed.

The Jaguars lead 23-3 in the fourth quarter after Cam Little's second-half field goals of 45 and 47 yards.

The Ravens had 25 yards and no first downs in the third quarter and have only 126 yards and seven first downs for the game.

item.title: Derrick Henry moves to seventh on the NFL's all-time rushing list
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Ravens running back passed Jerome Bettis (13,662) and LaDainian Tomlinson (13,684).
item.content:encoded:
The Ravens haven't had much to celebrate Thursday night, but Derrick Henry gave the home fans something to cheer.

Henry had 51 first-half rushing yards, which was enough to move him into seventh on the all-time rushing list. He passed Jerome Bettis (13,662) and LaDainian Tomlinson (13,684) in moving from ninth to seventh.

Curtis Martin is next on the list, with his 14,101 career rushing yards ranking sixth all time.

Henry entered the night with 632 yards for the season and 13,650 in his career.

Over the past four seasons, Henry has averaged 1,578 yards. He has averaged 85 yards per game in his career.

Henry will need to play another three to four years to break Emmitt Smith's record of 18,355 yards.

Smith was 35 years old in his final season of 2004. Henry turns 33 in January.

Smith said earlier this year that he believes Henry has a chance to break his record.

item.title: Thursday Night Football: Jaguars lead Ravens 17-3 at halftime
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence was 9-of-15 for 197 yards and a touchdown in the first half.
item.content:encoded:
The Ravens were hanging . . . until they weren't.

Baltimore was within one score with less than 2 minutes to play in the first half. But Parker Washington beat Malaki Starks, and after a bobble of Trevor Lawrence's pass, secured the catch and raced 50 yards for a touchdown with 58 seconds left in the half.

The Jaguars lead the Ravens 17-3 at halftime.

The Ravens started undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano with Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley on injured reserve. They opened the game with Derrick Henry in the wildcat and called seven plays out of the formation.

The Ravens had 17 runs and 12 passes as they shortened the half. Henry had 12 carries for 51 yards and threw a pass that lost 3 yards.

Zay Flowers had two rushes for 16 yards and two catches for 2 yards.

Fagnano, who lined up at quarterback for only 12 plays, was 7-of-11 for 30 yards.

The Jaguars outgained the Ravens 223 to 101, with Lawrence going 9-of-15 for 197 yards and a touchdown.

Running back Bhayshul Tuten, who was questionable to play with ankle and foot injuries, scored a 1-yard touchdown on the team's opening drive. He has 22 yards on eight carries.

Jakobi Meyers has four catches for 65 yards, with Washington adding two for 61 and rookie tight end Nate Boerkircher one for 52.

Linebacker Foyesade Oluokun leads the Jacksonville defense with six tackles and a sack.

The Ravens held the ball for 17:31 of the first 30 minutes.

item.title: Myles Garrett remains limited participant Thursday
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Rams outside linebacker Myles Garrett remained a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
item.content:encoded:
Rams outside linebacker Myles Garrett remained a limited participant in Thursday's practice. Garrett returned to practice Wednesday, his first practice since Week 1.

Garrett underwent arthroscopic knee surgery in mid-September after playing 40 snaps in the season opener. He was given a six-week prognosis and has missed seven games.

He and Aaron Donald could play together for the first time on Sunday when the Rams play the Commanders.

Quarterback Matthew Stafford (right elbow) was a full participant again.

The Rams had only two changes to their injury report: Inside linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring) did not practice after being limited Wednesday, and offensive lineman Steve Avila (hamstring) was a full participant a day after being limited.

The Rams again practiced without cornerback Jaylen Watson (shoulder), long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle), cornerback Trent McDuffie (back), tight end Colby Parkinson (ribs) and safety Kam Curl (foot).

Wide receiver Jordan Whittington (back) and tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle) remained limited.
